claim.name: M7-G canonical read-only fan-out capability and benefit audit
claim.primary_problem: The canonical runtime already launches multiple same-turn read-only children before joining them, but current evidence proves only event ordering. Historical multi-agent evidence contains exactly one child and cannot attribute any wall-time or task-success gain to fan-out.
claim.acceptance: Prove overlapping production HTTP requests, complete typed handoffs, shared accounting, cancellation/partial-failure behavior, and exact SQLite reopen. Then compare the same immutable binary on the same task prompt, model, total budget, and maximum_reruns=0 with the agent surface disabled versus exactly two explicitly admitted read-only children.
claim.single_owner: crates/runtime AgentRuntime owns child scheduling and join; crates/state RunStore owns durable truth; crates/app owns production composition; the evaluation harness may only project canonical Run API and event facts.
claim.replacement: No production path is replaced unless evidence identifies a concrete scheduler defect. The treatment uses the existing canonical agent tool and RunLimits only.
claim.cutover_deletion: If live admission or stable net benefit fails, delete any experiment-only production branch and retain only the contract test, frozen fixtures/manifest/result, and decision summary.

frozen_rules.provider_parallel_tool_call_switch: not documented; CodeWhale must not invent one
frozen_rules.reasoning_replay: reasoning_content is replayed exactly across tool-call turns

baseline_diagnosis.production_call_graph: AgentApplication -> AgentRuntime; every same-response agent call durably prepares and starts one child, read-only starts return immediately into pending_children, and join_children runs only after the complete tool-call batch.
baseline_diagnosis.join_order: pending children are durably settled in launch order even though their model requests may overlap.
baseline_diagnosis.shared_budget: root and every child reserve from one RuntimeBudget for model requests, tools, wall deadline, and child capacity.
baseline_diagnosis.reopen_contract: an uncollected read-only child at process loss fails closed as RecoveryRequired/ChildRun; it is never blindly restarted.

historical_evidence.conclusion: This evidence supports eager join mechanics only and contains no fan-out treatment.

offline_matrix: two same-turn read-only child HTTP requests are simultaneously in flight through AgentApplication production composition
both AgentTaskPrepared and ChildStarted events precede the first ChildFinished
each child has one canonical RunStore run and terminal outcome
both typed handoffs are present before one root integration request
root plus children share complete usage and request accounting
one child failure is returned without losing the sibling handoff
SQLite reopen reproduces exact root and child snapshots/events
process loss with an uncollected read-only child is RecoveryRequired and issues no duplicate model or tool side effect

experiment.pair_order: balanced alternating within each task/run index

metrics: tool calls and failed tool outcomes

decision_threshold.reliability: verified success must not decrease and false success must not increase
decision_threshold.fanout: every treatment arm must prove exactly two same-turn read-only children and complete handoffs
decision_threshold.efficiency: wall time must improve stably at pair and aggregate levels; added tokens, requests, and cost are explicit transfer costs and must not erase the verified-task gain
decision_threshold.complexity: no second runtime/store/model loop/tool catalog/product mode/general DAG or Writer concurrency
